If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
" *

Adds all the elements of the given arrays into a new array.

*

The new array contains all of the element of array1 followed * by all of the elements array2. When an array is returned, it is always * a new array.

* * 
     * ArrayUtils.addAll(null, null)     = null
     * ArrayUtils.addAll(array1, null)   = cloned copy of array1
     * ArrayUtils.addAll(null, array2)   = cloned copy of array2
     * ArrayUtils.addAll([], [])         = []
     * ArrayUtils.addAll([null], [null]) = [null, null]
     * ArrayUtils.addAll(["a", "b", "c"], ["1", "2", "3"]) = ["a", "b", "c", "1", "2", "3"]
     *
* * @param array1 the first array whose elements are added to the new array, may be null * @param array2 the second array whose elements are added to the new array, may be null * @return The new array, null if both arrays are null. * The type of the new array is the type of the first array, * unless the first array is null, in which case the type is the same as the second array. * @since 2.1 "

Diagnosis:
The failure is rooted in the method ArrayUtils.addAll(T[] array1, T... array2) in the Apache Commons Lang library. The method is intended to concatenate two arrays of the same generic component type into a new array.

The failing test validates two scenarios:
1. Adding an Integer array and Long array to a Number array, which works fine because Number is the common superclass.
2. Adding a Long array to an Integer array, which fails and raises an ArrayStoreException instead of the expected IllegalArgumentException.

From the code snippet:
- The method gets the runtime component type of the first array (type1).
- It then creates a new array instance of this type with the combined length.
- It copies the contents of array1 to the new array.
- Then it attempts to copy the contents of array2 to the new array using System.arraycopy.

The issue occurs because when the runtime type of array1 is Integer[], creating a new array of Integer[] type and then trying to copy Long[] elements into it causes an ArrayStoreException at runtime, as Java array store checks fail. This is a fundamental Java limitation with generic arrays and covariant types.

The method lacks explicit type compatibility checks to prevent this and instead relies on System.arraycopy, which throws a runtime exception that is not caught or transformed into a clearer exception like IllegalArgumentException as expected by the test.

The bug report highlights this problem and mentions that the current stack trace (ArrayStoreException) is not very clear, implying that the method should check array types before copying and throw a clearer exception if incompatible.

Recent bug reports do not relate directly to this issue.

In summary, the bug happens because ArrayUtils.addAll does not handle type mixing well when the arrays are of different component types that cannot coerce into the first array type, resulting in a runtime ArrayStoreException instead of a clear validation error.

The failing test expects an IllegalArgumentException, but the current implementation allows the ArrayStoreException from System.arraycopy to propagate.

This diagnosis aligns perfectly with the test and bug report's observations.
org.apache.commons.lang3.ArrayUtils.addAll(T[], T...)
